descriptions.job-01zn03m:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is hiring a People Strategy, M&A Lead to build a function that doesn't exist here today: how Ramp attracts, evaluates, prices, and closes the teams and companies that join us through an acquisition. This is a new role, and you'll build it from the ground up.

You'll own that work end to end. For team acquisitions, that means the pipeline, the assessment, the economics, the founder and team conversations, the offers, and post-close integration with People Operations and the hiring teams. When Ramp acquires a company outright, you'll own the people side of the deal alongside Corporate Development: who stays, at what level, on what terms, and how we communicate it.

You'll report to Ramp's head of People Finance & Strategy and work day to day with Corporate Development, Legal, and the business leaders who'll take the teams.

This is a senior individual contributor role with direct exposure to our co-founders, CFO, and head of Corporate Development. You'll run the hiring process yourself, from first conversation to signed offers, and stay with the team through post-close integration, which no one owns at Ramp today. The scope will change as we do more of this, and defining it is part of the job.

This role will grow with what Ramp does. As volume grows, so does the scope: larger acquisitions alongside Corporate Development, the people side of company acquisitions, and strategy work across People Finance & Strategy. At Ramp, people who have built deep operating judgment in roles like this have gone on to lead major business areas. For the right person, this is a way to build deal judgment and talent judgment at the same time, with the company context to take on broader operating roles over time in corporate development, general management, or People leadership.

You don't need to have done this exact job before. You do need to have run deals or searches yourself and be credible with founders and with executives.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the relationships. The founder, every member of the team, and the Ramp leaders who'd take them hear from you first, and you keep those conversations moving from the first call to signed offers.

  • Assess the team with the leaders who'd take it: who's essential, what roles and levels they'd hold at Ramp, and what it would take for them to join and stay.

  • Price and structure the package. Use market data and our compensation framework to build an offer for each person and a budget for the team, including salary, equity, sign-on, and retention.

  • Write the recommendation. Pursue, pass, or route to Corporate Development, with the economics compared to hiring the same people individually. Present it to our co-founders, CFO, and head of Corporate Development.

  • Run the process: interviews, references, light diligence, negotiation within agreed bounds, and close.

  • Build the pipeline with Corporate Development. Keep a current view of the companies and teams in the areas Ramp is building, and of the investors, founders, and bankers who see them early. Qualify quickly and pass quickly.

  • Handle the mechanics with Legal and People Operations: confidentiality, non-solicits, immigration, the team's existing equity, and timing.

  • Own post-close integration with People Operations and the hiring teams: start dates, managers, onboarding, retention checkpoints. Track whether the people we set out to hire joined, stayed, and performed, and turn what you learn into a playbook.

  • On company acquisitions, own the people workstream with Corporate Development: team diligence, leveling, retention design, offers, and communications.

 

What You Need

  • 6-10 years in venture capital, growth equity, corporate development, M&A advisory, management consulting, or executive search, including deals, searches, or client work you ran yourself.

  • Intellectual curiosity about Ramp and the space we operate in. You want to understand the business well enough to know which teams would make it better and why.

  • Extremely strong judgment. You can tell a strong team from a good pitch, and you know when to push, when to pass, and when to bring in Corporate Development or Legal.

  • Sourcing experience. You've found companies or people before they were introduced to you, and you can get a founder to take a call.

  • High emotional intelligence. You build trust quickly with founders and senior engineers, and you can deliver a hard answer without losing the relationship.

  • Comfort with executives. You can present a recommendation to a CEO with the full breakdown, handle pushback, and change your view when the facts change.

  • Financial fluency: cap tables, preference stacks, options and RSUs, and what each is worth to the person holding it.

  • Negotiation experience. The hard conversations in this job get solved with creativity, judgment, and structure, and you've done that yourself.

  • Integration experience. You've brought a team or company into a new organization and seen it through to people being productive.

  • Calm and structure. You can run several live opportunities at once and keep every thread moving.

  • Ambition and attitude. Low ego, high ownership, and the drive to build this into something Ramp relies on.

  • Discretion. Everything in this role is confidential, often on both sides of the table.

  • Ability to work onsite from Ramp's New York office three or more days per week.

     

Nice-to-Haves

  • You've been through an acquihire from either side.

  • You've run a search end to end.

  • Familiarity with compensation and equity design at a late-stage private company.

About Fin

Fin is a next-generation payments platform built for high-value, global, and instant transactions. We are a Series A-stage company backed by Sequoia, Circle, and other notable investors. Powered by stablecoins, Fin enables users and businesses to move millions of dollars in seconds - whether to other Fin users, directly into bank accounts, or across crypto rails. By combining the speed of crypto with the reliability and trust of traditional finance, Fin reimagines how money moves worldwide. If banks and payment products were reinvented today, they would look like Fin.

About the role

We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to own our day-to-day compliance processes and make them better as we scale.

Moving millions of dollars globally means our compliance engine has to be just as fast and reliable as our payment rails. In this role, you'll own how businesses get onboarded, how we manage risk across our platform, and how our internal tools evolve as payment volume grows.

At our stage, owning the product means being close to the work. You'll spend real time in our onboarding pipeline and monitoring queues—reviewing KYBs, sending RFIs, and triaging transaction alerts—so you can see firsthand where customers get stuck or where our workflows break down. From there, you'll work directly with engineering to automate manual steps, tune our tools, and build a smoother experience for both our customers and our team.

What you'll do

Own the Compliance Onboarding Flow

  • Manage the end-to-end compliance onboarding pipeline, tracking where every customer sits and making sure nothing stalls.

  • Jump into KYB reviews, send out RFIs, and follow up with customers to resolve open questions and make clear risk calls.

  • Redesign how we collect documents and communicate with businesses during onboarding so legitimate customers get approved faster without lowering our risk standards.

Build & Improve Internal Workflows

  • Work alongside engineering to turn repetitive compliance tasks into automated, auditable workflows.

  • Triage transaction monitoring and on-chain alerts to understand false positives, edge cases, and alert noise—then adjust rules, thresholds, and tooling to make monitoring sharper.

  • Own the roadmap for our compliance tooling stack (KYB, case management, and blockchain analytics) as we launch new features and payment corridors.

Track Performance & Keep the Program Moving

  • Define and monitor key metrics—like onboarding turnaround times, RFI response rates, and alert volumes—and use that data to decide what to fix next.

  • Coordinate across product, engineering, and external partners to support audits, partner requests, and new product launches.

  • Keep our internal processes documented and up to date as the way we work evolves.

What you bring

  • 1–4 years of experience in product management, product operations, bizops, or fintech/crypto operations.

  • High ownership. You like taking messy, manual processes and turning them into clean, repeatable systems.

  • Comfort getting in the weeds. You're willing to review a complex business application or dig into a flagged transaction yourself so you actually understand the problem before scoping a fix.

  • Clear, direct communication. You can write a straightforward RFI to a customer, a crisp spec for an engineer, and a solid summary for a banking partner.

  • Strong organizational habits. You can keep a busy customer pipeline and multiple engineering projects moving at the same time.

  • Familiarity with fintech or crypto compliance (KYB, AML, sanctions, or transaction monitoring), or the drive to ramp up on it quickly.

Nice to have

  • Experience working with tools like Persona, Middesk, Chainalysis, or TRM.

  • Background in payments, stablecoins, or B2B onboarding flows.

  • Experience partnering directly with engineers to ship internal tools or workflow automations.

It all started with an idea at Block in 2013. Initially built to take the pain out of peer-to-peer payments, Cash App has gone from a simple product with a single purpose to a dynamic ecosystem, developing unique financial products, including Afterpay/Clearpay, to provide a better way to send, spend, invest, borrow and save to our 50+ million monthly active customers. Today, Cash App has thousands of employees working globally across office and remote locations, with a culture geared toward innovation, collaboration and impact. We’ve been a distributed team since day one, and many of our roles can be done remotely from the countries where Cash App operates. No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.

The Role

The Advanced Insights and Modeling (AIM) team is a high-impact, business-savvy group of builders: machine learning engineers, data scientists, data engineers, and business strategists who combine technical skills with deep product and financial expertise. We hold high standards, move fast, and own our models end to end. AIM runs on curiosity, bold thinking, and collaboration, and we keep the culture decidedly non-corporate. Teams across Block come to us when they need insight, speed, and real business impact.

AIM sits within Block’s Foundational organization and is sponsored directly by the CFO, but our mandate runs well beyond Finance. We own most of the measurement and predictive modeling at Block: forecasting across Cash App, Square, and Afterpay, customer lifetime value, marketing incrementality and spend optimization, sales pipeline and prospect value, and actives and network-effect measurement. Finance, Marketing, Sales, Product, and Risk all plan against numbers we produce. We also own the data foundations those models run on, and corporate functions including Finance, Accounting, Treasury, SFS, and Procurement increasingly come to us when they want to rethink how their work gets done with AI.

Automation across the enterprise. AIM leads Block’s Foundational Automation program, a CFO-sponsored effort to rebuild how Finance, Accounting, Treasury, SFS, and Procurement operate. Rather than layering AI on top of existing workflows, we rebuild the underlying data and process layer so that agents can take on the work itself: monitoring pipelines, reconciling positions, triaging exceptions, and escalating only the decisions that need a person. In Treasury, you will define and build the data systems and controls that make this automation reliable.

The Treasury opportunity. Block moves money through hundreds of bank accounts across multiple legal entities, and Treasury’s view of that position today is stitched together from bank portals, a liquidity tool, portfolio accounting, and the general ledger, with the gaps closed by hand. No single system tells Treasury, in near real time, where every dollar sits and whether the books agree. You will build that system from the ground up.

Your mandate. You will own the technical direction and hands-on development of Treasury’s data foundation. Treasury manages Block’s own cash, liquidity, and investments across its businesses and legal entities. You will work directly with Treasury and Accounting to understand how they operate, identify what needs to change, and turn those needs into a technical roadmap.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will make architecture and build-versus-buy recommendations, decide what to tackle first, and personally build and operate the core data systems. We’re looking for someone who can take an open-ended business problem through to a working solution, bringing clear recommendations when decisions need broader agreement.

Treasury is the first function to get this treatment. The architecture, controls, and operating model you establish will become the template for Accounting, Procurement, and the rest of Foundational.

Your initial priorities. You will shape the roadmap around three connected needs:

  • A trusted liquidity position. Bring bank, custodian, portfolio accounting, and general ledger data into a reliable entity-level view in Snowflake. Define the architecture, reconciliation approach, and data quality controls, then build the pipelines and data models.
  • A foundation for forecasting. Partner with AIM’s ML engineers to establish the datasets, features, and data contracts for predicting cash inflows and outflows. Own the underlying data systems through production.
  • A clear direction for Treasury systems. Lead the technical recommendation for Block’s 2027 Treasury Management System decision: what to build, what to buy, and how the pieces should fit together. Define the integration and migration approach for the chosen direction.

You will determine the sequencing and trade-offs with Treasury and AIM.

Success means Treasury uses and trusts the systems you build, forecasting has reliable inputs, and manual reconciliation and investigation require less effort. Your initial focus is Treasury. Over time, the role can expand within across AIM’s broader portfolio, including forecasting infrastructure, customer-level data products, and GTM measurement.

You Will

  • Personally design, build, and operate the Treasury liquidity datamart in Snowflake, including source integrations, data models, reconciliation logic, and data contracts.
  • Partner with AIM’s ML engineers on liquidity forecasting, building and maintaining the reliable datasets and pipelines those models depend on.

  • Own production reliability and controls, including data quality, lineage, access, recovery, and on-call. Build automation, including AI agents where appropriate, to reduce manual monitoring and investigation while preserving necessary human review.

About Sapiom

Sapiom is building payment infrastructure for AI agents. We enable agents to make purchases for people, manage payments between businesses, and buy the compute, inference, and APIs they need to operate. As agents become part of everyday life, we're building toward the experiences people will use to trust them with their money: one place to set what agents can do, see what they did, and stay in control across every agent they use.

Through one integration, Sapiom connects agents to funding sources and payment methods. Our intent verification checks that each transaction matches what the person or business authorized. Spending controls define where and how much agents can spend, with a record of every transaction and its outcome. We're building toward a world where people and businesses can delegate payments to agents with confidence.

We're a small team in San Francisco with deep experience in payments and infrastructure. Our founder was Director of Engineering in Payments at Shopify for five years. We've raised $50 million in our first 12 months from Accel, Dragonfly, Coinbase Ventures, Okta Ventures, Menlo Ventures and Anthropic.

Agents are starting to act and transact on their own, and the products that make people comfortable trusting them are still being invented. This is a chance to shape how the world works with agents. You'll be our first product manager, owning product from framing the problem through launch with our founder, engineering and design. Controls are the facility's nervous system: when they fail or mislead, operators lose sight of everything else.

Operability Design Review
Review controls designs, including BMS/BAS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC-based plant controls, CDU and cooling plant controls, and generator, UPS, and switchgear controller integration, through an operations lens. Sequences of operations, failure-mode and fail-safe behavior, loss-of-network and loss-of-controller response, manual and local override, point lists and instrumentation adequacy, alarm philosophy and prioritization, graphics clarity, and OT network architecture and access control. Push back where the design assumes an operator will understand or recover something the system never tells them.


Controls QA/QC and Vendor Oversight
Provide QA/QC oversight of controls scope for new construction and retrofits: review vendor proposals and programming, directly oversee system configuration and component upgrades, and witness factory tests. Hold controls vendors to Hut 8 standards and to the approved sequences, and make sure every modification to a system follows change control.


Construction-Phase Verification
Walk controls installations at key milestones. Flag operability and quality issues to the MEP superintendent early, while they are still cheap to fix.


Commissioning
Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of controls and automation: point-to-point verification, sequence- of-operations testing, controller, server, and network failover, alarm verification, trend validation, and integrated systems testing across mechanical, electrical, and controls, including loss-of- communication and loss-of-BMS scenarios. Review programming through the commissioning process, drive operational findings into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria, and verify closure personally.


Turnover Readiness
Verify controls turnover packages: as-built sequences of operation, point lists, control and network drawings, programming backups and configuration files under version control, licenses and credentials transferred to Hut 8, alarm setpoint and priority matrices, trend baselines, spare controllers and critical modules, and PM program inputs such as backup routines, firmware updates, and panel power health. Confirm the backups actually restore.


Training
Provide technical controls training and support to Facility Operations staff, and validate that operator training equips the team to use the systems, not just look at them.


Program Feedback
Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 controls standards, point naming and alarm conventions, and the next project's basis of design, and work with other Hut 8 sites and teams to carry standards across the portfolio.
